result.title: Attack-Inference Aligned Universal Adversarial Attacks on Video Object Segmentation
result.summary: Modern video object segmentation (VOS) relies on a two-stage inference paradigm: target initialization and memory-based propagation. However, existing adversarial attacks on VOS often overlook this structure. To bridge this gap, we propose AUV, an adversarial framework that Aligns with the Universal two-stage paradigm of VOS models. Specifically, AUV optimizes a universal adversarial perturbation (UAP) through decoupled training strategies tailored for both initialization and propagation stages. By disrupting the shared memory space, it achieves prompt-agnostic attacks across different modalities, including masks, points, boxes, and language. Extensive experiments show that AUV establishes state-of-the-art VOS attack performance, such as degrading mask-based SAM3 to only 8.4 J&F on DAVIS17-val (compared to 55.4 for the previous SOTA under the same training setup). It also exhibits superior temporal dynamics with the fastest onset, the most enduring persistence, and the support of any-time mid-video attacks. The AUV optimization framework is applicable to different VOS models, revealing vulnerabilities in real-world streaming VOS. Code is available at https://github.com/FudanCVL/AUV.

AI.brief_summary: 该文提出 AUV，针对 VOS 的两阶段推理（目标初始化与基于记忆的传播）分别设计解耦训练策略，优化通用对抗扰动以破坏共享记忆空间，从而实现对掩码、点、框、语言等多种提示模态的 prompt-agnostic 攻击，并在多个 VOS 模型上取得更优攻击效果。
AI.relevance_reason: 破坏共享记忆空间相当于对「视觉证据是否被保存并实际使用」做扰动式干预，可能为核查 LVR 中视觉细节留存与信息坍缩提供探针思路；但论文面向分割攻击而非推理状态，迁移价值需阅读原文核查。
